title.narrative: Output 1.4. Increased capacity of Member States to improve social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative: 1. During 2022-23, the Labour Dispute Resolution systems in three provinces/city (Binh Duong, Dong Nai and Ho Chi Minh city) have been consolidated and administratively streamlined in line with the requirements of the new Labour Code 2019. In all 3 provinces, the new institutional arrangements include the appointment of dispute management focal points establishment of tripartite Labour Arbitration Councils (LAC) have been established to resolve labour disputes. 2. Capacity and effectiveness for dispute prevention and resolution at provincial levels improved during the biennium through developing working regulations of, and training mediators and arbitrators on new legal provisions, dispute resolution processes, mediation and arbitration skills – it improved access to dispute resolution services. As an initial outcome, the first-ever arbitration case was received and resolved by the LAC of Dong Nai in November 2022. 3. The effective and timely tripartite social dialogues at different levels (national, sectoral, enterprises focussed on garment and footwear industries) organized by the VCCI/Business Associations for exchanging good practices, sharing knowledge, and providing solutions among the public-private partners to support the speedy recovery of the business after Covid 19, while ensuring the workforce health and safety in the post-Covid recovery of 2022-23. 1. With the support from the government of USA and European Union, ILO provided support to the social dialogue processes and capacity building of constituents in the three provinces to – develop work plans to consolidate dispute resolution systems in line with the provisions of the new labour code, set up focal point units for dispute resolution, streamlined processes and develop technical guidelines for selection and training of mediators and arbitrators. During the biennium, 269 mediators and 48 arbitrators were trained [31% are female]

Output 7.3. Increased capacity of Member States to set adequate wages and promote decent working time

description.narrative: 1. To improve the evidence base for setting adequate wages, taking into account both the needs of the workers and their families and economic factors, the Ministry of Labour, Invalids, and Social Affairs (MOLISA) has officially released its first-ever National Wage Report, reviewing wage structures and trends across the country, fostering a better understanding of wage dynamics, as well as for improving the informed decision-making. The report was shared with all members of the National Wage Council and used as evidence for the decision that was made in August 2023 to increase the minimum wage rate in 2024. 2. To increase minimum wage compliance and effectiveness for part-time workers, including in the informal economy, the hourly minimum wage was officially adopted in Viet Nam through decree 38/ND-CP issued 12 June 2022, and effective from 1 July 2022. This complements the existing monthly minimum wage which applies primarily to workers with full-time monthly arrangements. 1. With funding from the Government of the Netherlands, the ILO supported the publication of the National Wage Report, with a view to strengthening the use of data and indicators in existing wage-setting mechanisms. The ILO supported the production by MOLISA of the National Wage Report with technical inputs, a series of technical consultations on methodologies that were used in the report, as well as a peer review of the draft report. Furthermore, the ILO provided support to the dissemination of the report and supported a public information campaign on the minimum wage system during the 10th anniversary of the National Wage Council. The ILO also provided technical inputs to the meetings of the National Wage Council. Technical inputs by the ILO (including the ILO Policy Brief on minimum wage responses to the cost-of-living crisis) informed the recommendations of the National Wage Council to increase the minimum wage in 2024. 2. The ILO supported the adoption of an hourly minimum wage, including with a technical workshop in December 17, 2021, followed up by virtual meetings responding to questions on the implementation in January 2022. Drawing from country experiences with different minimum wage systems (hourly, weekly and monthly), the ILO produced technical notes that were used in the deliberations about the modalities of the hourly minimum wage, addressing amongst others the question of how the hourly minimum wage should be calculated.

Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity and resilience of labour administrations

description.narrative: During 2022-23, the Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs together with three targeted provincial Departments of Labour, Invalid and Social Affair (Ho Chi Minh City, Dong Nai, and Binh Duong) developed an initial version of an Electronic Case Management System (ECMS) to streamline work process and improve the efficiency and data collection of the labour inspection system in Viet Nam. The ECMS includes sector-based digital checklists to standardize field inspections, a sanctions module to help automate violation findings and measures, a data analysis and report module to improve objective-based planning and performance monitoring, as well as to facilitate Viet Nam’s reporting on the application of ILO Convention No. 81. The system is considered as one of the solutions to advance the labour inspection system in Vietnam, which recognized in the « Building capacity for the labour – Invalids and Social Affairs Inspection Sector » Action Plan for 2021-2025. The first version of ECMS was piloted in late 2022 with mock inspection visits to 10 selected enterprises. Feedback from users – labour inspectors and managers of labour inspectorates – were collected and analyzed for software upgrading. The ECMS is well aligned with the stated priorities of Vietnam’s Government, with a centralized, structured database that would help improve the supervision and transparency of inspection cases and their progress, and both national and provincial levels would benefit from the analysis of this data. This work also led to improved inter-ministerial collaboration between the Ministry Inspectorate, the Department of Work Safety, and the Information Technology Department as a foundation for the shared ownership and viability of the system. The ECMC could help to improve coverage and quality of inspection services, as stated by the leader of the Ministry's Inspection. The ILO with support from the government of USA developed the ECMS. The ILO facilitated the collaboration between different Ministry Departments through different mechanisms, such as frequent management meetings, HelpDesk and technical group meetings, and training. The communication and collaboration between national and provincial levels is also built up through promoting the application of participatory principles.

Output 1.4. Increased capacity of Member States to improve social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative: The technical and organizational capacity of the National Industrial Relations Committee (NIRC), an apex level tripartite body, strengthened to address not only the current and emerging industrial relations challenges facing constituents in Vietnam but also to develop guidelines and regular reporting. During this biennium, the NIRC was reinforced through the Prime Minister's Decision, with full functions and a plan of action, including the endorsement of the relevant reports, technical guidelines, and recommendations for the improvement of industrial relations at both national and sub-national levels. 1. With funding from Canada, ILO provided technical support to social dialogue processes, introduced international experiences to strengthen the capacity building of NIRC, of the constituents, supported the design and development of the NIRC agenda, and supported the development of regular National IR Report and NIRC recommendations, etc. 2. With support from Canada, the ILO facilitated knowledge development processes, provided technical support to constituents in tripartite and bipartite social dialogue processes to build consensus on policy, and promoted capacity building through various training programmes on Social Dialogue & Collective Bargaining for trade unions, enterprises and HR.
